vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: book-anything
Version: 1.4.1

The 'book-anything' skill provides a legitimate service for searching businesses and making AI-powered phone bookings via the LifeClaw API (api-v2.lifeclaw.agentese.ai). The documentation in SKILL.md and references/api.md outlines a standard, well-structured REST API workflow including authentication via a Bearer token, search, detail retrieval, and task polling. No indicators of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or harmful prompt injection were found.

llm.summary: The skill's runtime instructions line up with a phone-booking service that needs a LifeClaw API token, but the package metadata omits the required credential and the skill will send user PII to a third-party API via a Telegram-issued token — this mismatch and privacy exposure merit caution.

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md describes a service that searches businesses and places bookings via an external LifeClaw REST API using an API token — this is coherent with the name/description. However, the registry metadata provided earlier listed no required environment variables while SKILL.md explicitly requires LIFECLAW_API_TOKEN. That metadata inconsistency is unexpected and should be corrected or explained by the publisher.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions are limited to calling the LifeClaw API endpoints and polling for results — no local file or system access is requested. However, to perform bookings the agent is instructed to send user-identifying data (name, contact_phone, possibly special_requests and predicted Q/A) to the remote API. That is expected for a booking service, but it means the skill will transmit PII to api-v2.lifeclaw.agentese.ai and to a Telegram bot (for token creation). The SKILL.md does not warn about data/PII handling or retention.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is instruction-only with no install spec or code files to execute locally. That minimizes on-host risk (nothing is written/installed by the skill).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The only declared runtime credential in SKILL.md is LIFECLAW_API_TOKEN (required) which is proportional to a third-party API integration. Two concerns: (1) the registry metadata listed no required env vars despite SKILL.md requiring a token, and (2) the token is created via a Telegram bot (@lifeclaw_ai_bot) and shown only once — users should verify the bot and service are trustworthy before storing/using the token.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true, has no install steps that modify other skills or system-wide config, and is user-invocable only. It does not demand persistent elevated privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing or enabling this skill, consider the following: (1) Verify the publisher and the domain api-v2.lifeclaw.agentese.ai and confirm @lifeclaw_ai_bot on Telegram is the official token-issuer — token creation via Telegram is unusual and could be spoofed. (2) Expect the skill to send users' names, phone numbers, booking details, and any other input you provide to a third-party service; do not send sensitive personal data unless you trust the service and its privacy policy. (3) The registry metadata mismatch (it lists no required env vars while SKILL.md requires LIFECLAW_API_TOKEN) should be corrected by the author — ask for clarification. (4) Review pricing and point-based costs (phone calls billed per minute) to avoid unexpected charges. (5) If you need stronger privacy guarantees, request the vendor's data-retention and security policy or use a throwaway/test account/token first. If the publisher cannot explain the metadata mismatch or the Telegram token process, treat the skill as untrusted.
